title: gRPC agent transport depends on a WASM module whose output dir is empty; grpc path silently no-ops
defect: openGrpcAgentStream dynamically imports 'frf-wasm'; when unavailable loadWasm() returns null and the function returns early (line 92 `if (!wasm) return;`) after Vite's stub plugin (vite.config.ts) replaces the module with a throw-only stub because wasm-pack output is not present. The connection status is left as-is with no error surfaced.
failure_scenario: An operator toggles the Agent panel transport to 'gRPC (WASM)'. Because the frf-wasm binary was never built, the stream open silently returns without connecting or reporting failure — the panel shows a stale status and no events, with no indication to the user that the transport is a no-op. Even when built, this path targets the same browser-unreachable tonic server (see finding 1).
evidence: agentGrpcStream.ts:60-70 loadWasm catch returns null; :92 `if (!wasm) return;`; vite.config.ts frfWasmStubPlugin returns a stub that throws 'frf-wasm not built'; CrdtDemoButton.tsx error text 'is frf-wasm built? Run: bash crates/frf-wasm/build_wasm.sh'.
verify_reason:
The finding's control-flow observation is real but its stated preconditions are factually false in this checkout, and its cross-reference is wrong.

CONFIRMED (code-level): agentGrpcStream.ts:60-61 does `const wasm = await loadWasm(); if (!wasm) return;` BEFORE any store write (setConnectionStatus("connecting") is at line 64). loadWasm() (lines 27-42) swallows any error/throw in its catch and returns null. So if the WASM module is genuinely absent, openGrpcAgentStream returns silently with connectionStatus left at its default "disconnected" (agentEventStore.ts:27) and no error surfaced. That is a real silent-fallback UX defect.

FALSE as characterized — the auditor's triggering scenario does not hold:
1. "output dir is empty / wasm was never built" is WRONG. sdks/ts/frf-wasm/ contains built artifacts: frf_wasm_bg.wasm (2.2MB) and frf_wasm.js (built Jun 21 16:20), and admin-ui/node_modules/frf-wasm symlinks to it.
2. "Vite's stub plugin replaces the module with a throw-only stub" is WRONG here. frfWasmStubPlugin (vite.config.ts) does `require.resolve("frf-wasm")`; because the symlink resolves, wasmAvailable=true and the plugin returns an inert `{ name: "frf-wasm-stub" }` — the throw-only stub (resolveId/load) is NOT installed. The dynamic import resolves the real module.
3. "targets the same browser-unreachable tonic server (finding 1)" is WRONG. crates/frf-wasm/src/agent.rs opens the stream via fetch() with Content-Type application/connect+json and Connect-Protocol-Version: 1 to /flint.v1.AgentService/RunAgent — i.e. the Connect protocol over HTTP POST, which IS browser-reachable. It is not raw tonic/grpc.

Net: with the module present (its actual state), toggling to gRPC loads the real WASM AgentStream and attempts a real Connect POST; the "silent no-op" path is not exercised. The residual real defect (silent return with stale status) only manifests if the built artifact is deleted, and even then it is a minor UX/observability gap, not a MEDIUM production hole. Corrected severity: LOW.

title: LICENSE declared as MIT in Cargo.toml but no LICENSE file exists
defect: The workspace manifest sets `license = "MIT"` and README says 'MIT (workspace default)', but there is no LICENSE/LICENSE-MIT file anywhere in the repo.
failure_scenario: Publishing crates to crates.io or open-sourcing the repo without a LICENSE file means the MIT grant is unenforceable/ambiguous; `cargo publish` will warn about the missing license file, and downstream consumers have no legal text to rely on, blocking any external adoption or distribution.
evidence: Cargo.toml:31 `license = "MIT"`; README.md:246 'MIT (workspace default). Confirm before first publish.'; `find . -iname 'LICENSE*'` returns nothing (excluding node_modules/target).
verify_reason: The finding is factually REAL and correctly characterized on the evidence: Cargo.toml:31 declares `license = "MIT"`, README.md:246 says "MIT (workspace default). Confirm before first publish.", all 22 crates inherit it via `license.workspace = true`, and no LICENSE/LICENSE-MIT/COPYING file exists anywhere in the repo (excluding node_modules/target). No crate sets `publish = false`, so every crate is nominally publishable. However, CRITICAL is over-stated for two reasons. (1) Technical: `cargo publish` does NOT hard-fail on a missing license *file* when a valid SPDX `license` expression is present — the SPDX `license` field is the standard, legally-meaningful mechanism and is enough for cargo; a missing full-text file yields at most a soft warning, so the claim that it "blocks any external adoption or distribution" is inaccurate. (2) Severity: this is a legal/packaging-hygiene gap, not a "security vulnerability or data-loss risk" (the project's own CRITICAL definition). It has zero runtime, connection, or security impact — nothing breaks in a production *deployment*; it only matters at the first-publish / open-source boundary, which the README itself already flags as a pending pre-publish TODO. Appropriate rating is LOW: a real documentation/packaging omission worth fixing before open-sourcing (add LICENSE-MIT with the standard MIT text), but not a release blocker for the running system.

title: README quickstart `cargo run -p frf-gateway` fails on clean checkout — mandatory env vars undocumented
defect: GatewayConfig::from_env() hard-requires IGGY_CONNECTION_STRING and GATEWAY_JWKS_URL with no defaults, but README's documented command `cargo run -p frf-gateway` provides no env and no doc lists the required set.

evidence: config.rs:117-118 `IGGY_CONNECTION_STRING ... .context("IGGY_CONNECTION_STRING must be set")?`; config.rs:125-126 same for GATEWAY_JWKS_URL; README.md:173 `cargo run -p frf-gateway` with no preceding env setup.
verify_reason: The technical claim is REAL and accurately cited. Verified at crates/frf-gateway/src/config.rs: line 117-118 IGGY_CONNECTION_STRING is required via std::env::var(...).context("IGGY_CONNECTION_STRING must be set")? with no default; line 125-126 GATEWAY_JWKS_URL is likewise required with no default. Both use `?` in from_env(), so the process exits immediately on a clean checkout. If anything the auditor UNDERCOUNTED: KETO_BASE_URL (line 120) and JWT_AUDIENCE (line 128) are ALSO mandatory with no defaults, so four env vars must be set, not two. README:173 does show `cargo run -p frf-gateway` under a bare `# Run gateway` comment with no preceding env setup, and there is no env-var reference anywhere (no .env.example, no env docs in README, no env table in docs/). So a developer following that line hits `IGGY_CONNECTION_STRING must be set` with no recovery doc.\n\nHowever, HIGH severity is overstated. (1) This is a pure documentation/onboarding gap, not a code bug, security hole, or broken-connection/data-loss defect — the code behaves CORRECTLY by fail-fast validating required secrets at startup (which the project's own Rust security rules explicitly recommend). (2) The auditor frames README:173 as a 'quickstart' / 'documented getting-started path', but it is actually one line in a terse 'Common Commands' reference list, not a step-by-step Getting Started tutorial that promises a running system — the framing inflates the contract the README makes. Per the project's own severity rubric this is a MEDIUM 'maintainability/onboarding concern' (INFO — consider fixing), not a HIGH 'bug or significant quality issue' that should warn/block a merge.

title: No environment-variable reference — ~30 gateway env vars are entirely undocumented
defect: The gateway/adapters read ~30 distinct env vars (auth, broker, CDC, LiveKit secrets, Matrix tokens, OTEL, Keto) but no doc enumerates them, their defaults, required-vs-optional status, or security sensitivity; only GATEWAY_JWKS_URL appears incidentally in one prose line of IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.

evidence: grep found 30 distinct env vars across crates (ATPROTO_*, CDC_*, DEV_NO_AUTH, GATEWAY_JWKS_URL, IGGY_CONNECTION_STRING, JWT_AUDIENCE, KETO_*, LIVEKIT_API_KEY/SECRET, MATRIX_*, OTEL_*, POLICY_ENGINE, SFU_MODE, REGISTRY_*); no .env.example and no env reference table in README or docs/.
verify_reason: REAL finding, correctly characterized; HIGH sustained. Verified against source: (1) docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:71 is a "Port map" table, not env docs — the file mentions env vars only incidentally (CDC troubleshooting line 98; Stage 10 notes) with no defaults/required/secret classification. (2) grep confirms ~29 distinct app env vars read across crates (auth: GATEWAY_JWKS_URL, JWT_AUDIENCE, DEV_NO_AUTH; broker: IGGY_CONNECTION_STRING; KETO_BASE_URL/NAMESPACE; 6 CDC_*; 4 LIVEKIT_* incl. LIVEKIT_API_SECRET; 3 MATRIX_* incl. MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN; 2 ATPROTO_*; 2 OTEL_*; POLICY_ENGINE, SFU_MODE, BIND_ADDR, GRPC_PORT, registry timers). (3) No .env/.env.example exists anywhere; README.md has ZERO env mentions; IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN references GATEWAY_JWKS_URL exactly once (line 255, a prose data-flow line); no env reference table exists in any doc. Required vars only surface as runtime .context() failures at startup (config.rs:118-128), with no upfront enumeration. (4) DEV_NO_AUTH is a genuine auth bypass (config.rs:65-70, publish.rs:57, subscribe.rs:56) and all three compose files set DEV_NO_AUTH:"true"; compose.yml also builds with CARGO_FEATURES=dev-endpoints, so an operator copying the documented "full stack" compose.yml as a prod baseline ships a live auth bypass with no doc warning it is dangerous. Two nuances that do NOT lower severity: the file:line anchor (DEVELOPMENT.md:71) is imprecise — it labels the port-map table rather than the missing env section, though the named defect is accurate — and DEV_NO_AUTH is compile-gated behind #[cfg(feature="dev-endpoints")], so a stock default-feature `cargo build --release` cannot honor it (a mitigating factor the prior auditor did not credit). Even so, an undocumented, secret-bearing config surface (LIVEKIT_API_SECRET, MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN) with a compose-enabled bypass flag is a legitimate production-readiness gap. Not CRITICAL (no code defect; worst case blocked in stock release build), clearly above MEDIUM given secret + bypass exposure. HIGH is correct.

title: No security-model document for a system whose whole premise is sovereign auth/tenant isolation
defect: There is no docs/SECURITY.md or security-model doc despite JWT verification (flint-gate/JWKS), Keto Zanzibar tenant isolation, Cedar action policy, per-event RLS, and a DEV_NO_AUTH bypass flag — the security model lives only scattered in CLAUDE.md and ADR-002.
failure_scenario: A security reviewer or operator has no single authoritative doc describing the trust boundary (where JWTs are verified, what DEV_NO_AUTH disables, how tenant isolation is enforced, the ADR-002 decision to skip per-event Keto checks on the agent bus), so a deployment may weaken the boundary (e.g., expose dev-endpoints or DEV_NO_AUTH) without understanding the consequences, and no SECURITY.md means no vulnerability-disclosure channel for a production service.
evidence: `find docs -iname '*security*'` returns nothing; DEV_NO_AUTH read in gateway with no doc; ADR-002 documents the per-event RLS deviation but is an ADR, not a consolidated security model.
verify_reason:
The factual claims are all verified and correct. `find docs -iname '*security*'` returns nothing; there is no docs/SECURITY.md or any SECURITY.md anywhere in the repo (only DEVELOPMENT.md, IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md, PROMETHEUS-BASE-RULES.md, and docs/decisions/ containing adr-001-crdt-engine.md and adr-002-agent-bus-tenant-isolation.md). No doc contains "trust boundary", "threat model", "security model", or "vulnerability disclosure". DEV_NO_AUTH is real: read in crates/frf-gateway/src/config.rs:66-70 and applied at subscribe.rs:56 / publish.rs:57. ADR-002 documents the per-event RLS deviation but is an ADR, not a consolidated security model. So the finding is REAL — a genuine production-release gap (no vuln-disclosure channel, no single authoritative trust-boundary doc for a sovereign-auth system).

However, HIGH overstates it. This is a documentation/operational-readiness gap, not a code defect. The trust boundary IS actually enforced in code: JWT verification runs in production, and the DEV_NO_AUTH bypass is compile-gated behind `#[cfg(feature = "dev-endpoints")]` (config.rs:60-70) — the function literally does not exist in production builds, so it cannot be invoked unless an operator deliberately compiles with the dev-endpoints feature. The failure scenario ("a deployment may weaken the boundary") is therefore indirect and operator-misconfiguration-dependent, not a live vulnerability. Per the project's own rubric (CLAUDE.md/code-review.md): HIGH = "Bug or significant quality issue"; MEDIUM = "Maintainability concern." A missing consolidated security doc — where the boundary is enforced in code and the one notable deviation is already captured in ADR-002 — is a MEDIUM maintainability/operational-readiness concern, not a HIGH bug.

title: No deployment/operations runbook for a multi-service production deployment

verify_reason: Verified against the actual repo. `find docs` for deploy/ops/runbook/production/operate/sre patterns returns nothing. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md is entirely local-dev focused — its section headers are Prerequisites, Local development, Full compose stack, Port map, CDC slot smoke test, WASM build, Layer 3 E2E, and ADRs; there is no production topology, secret provisioning, scaling, upgrade/rollback, or observability wiring section. README.md has Current State / Repo Structure / Architecture / Stack / SDK Strategy but no deployment or ops section. No k8s/Helm/Terraform/systemd/Nomad manifests exist anywhere — deploy/ holds only 3 undocumented config files (deploy/flint-gate/config.yaml, deploy/keto/keto.yml, deploy/postgres/init.sql) and there is a single bare Dockerfile with no deployment doc. Production is mentioned only once (DEVELOPMENT.md:172) as a throwaway note that prod images built without CARGO_FEATURES omit the dev endpoint — which itself references per-plane feature compilation yet gives zero guidance on which features to compile per plane, reinforcing the gap. For a system that wires Iggy, Keto, flint-gate, SurrealDB, Postgres logical replication, plus SFU/bridges, an SRE would have no production runbook. title: 21 of 22 crates have zero crate-level doc comments; no per-crate READMEs
defect: Only frf-ffi has module-level `//!` docs (8 lines); the other 21 crates (including frf-domain, frf-ports, frf-gateway, frf-crdt, all adapters) have zero `//!` crate docs and there are no per-crate README files.

evidence: Per-crate `//!` count: frf-ffi=8, all other 21 crates=0; `find crates -iname 'README*'` returns nothing.
verify_reason: Core factual claim is TRUE and correctly evidenced. Confirmed: crates/frf-domain/src/lib.rs:1 has `#![deny(warnings)]` (an inner attribute, no `//!` crate doc); of 22 crate dirs, 20 have ZERO `//!` anywhere in src, and `find crates -iname 'README*'` returns nothing (no per-crate READMEs).
